title: Flood Insurance: Flood Re (UK) and NFIP (US) Explained
description: How flood cover works: Flood Re for UK homes built before 2009, the US National Flood Insurance Program, private flood cover and waiting periods.
intro: Whether flood is included in your home insurance depends on where you live. In the UK it’s normally part of standard cover; in the US it almost never is. Here’s how to make sure you’re protected.

sections.html: Flood Re is a joint government and insurance industry reinsurance scheme that lets insurers offer more affordable flood cover to eligible households in high-risk areas. You don’t buy from Flood Re directly: you buy home insurance from an insurer that uses the scheme. Broadly, eligible homes are residential, insured by individuals, and built before 1 January 2009; some landlord, leasehold and commercial arrangements are excluded. The scheme is designed to end in 2039, with the aim of moving to risk-reflective pricing. Use Flood Re’s own eligibility checker for your home. More in Flood Re explained.

sections.h2: The US National Flood Insurance Program
sections.html:
The NFIP, managed by FEMA, offers flood insurance for buildings and contents in participating communities, sold through insurance agents and companies. Residential limits are up to $250,000 for the building and $100,000 for contents. Policies usually take effect after a 30-day waiting period. If your home is in a high-risk Special Flood Hazard Area and has a federally backed mortgage, flood insurance is required.

The NFIP depends on Congress for reauthorization, which has been extended many times in short bursts. As of mid-October 2026 it’s authorized until 11 December 2026. See what an NFIP lapse would mean. Private flood insurers are an alternative in many states and may offer higher limits.

• Sign up for official flood warnings (Environment Agency in England, SEPA, Natural Resources Wales; NOAA and local alerts in the US).
  • Consider property flood resilience measures such as flood doors, non-return valves and raised sockets.
  • Keep a flood plan and important documents in a waterproof bag.
  • Some UK insurers offer “Build Back Better” funding to add resilience measures after a flood claim.

faqs.q: Is flood covered by UK home insurance?
faqs.a: Normally yes, as part of standard buildings and contents cover. In high-risk areas it may be harder to find, which is where Flood Re helps eligible homes.

faqs.q: Does US homeowners insurance cover floods?
faqs.a: No. Standard homeowners, renters and condo policies exclude flood. Buy NFIP or private flood insurance separately, ideally well before storm season because of waiting periods.

faqs.q: Is my new-build home eligible for Flood Re?
faqs.a: Homes built on or after 1 January 2009 are not eligible, which is meant to discourage building in flood-prone areas.
